entrypoints.summary: A database-authorized user submits a SQL command through POST /api/v1/command/<db> that defines a function with LANGUAGE js, then invokes it using SELECT x.run().

capabilities.concept: SQL-defined JavaScript execution without scripting authorization

mitigations.concept: Centralized UPDATE_SECURITY authorization for all user-code execution surfaces
Disabled polyglot I/O and host access

impact.affected_asset: ArcadeDB database service authorization boundary and service network/resource availability.
impact.attacker_capability: A database-authorized non-security-admin can define and invoke arbitrary JavaScript through SQL.
impact.security_effect: Bypass of the authorization control intended to limit scripting to security administrators, with advisory-described SSRF/remote-script inclusion and CPU or memory denial-of-service exposure through permitted JavaScript loading/execution facilities.

causal_trace.summary: A user authorized for the target database, including a read-only role, supplies a SQL DEFINE FUNCTION statement whose body is JavaScript and declares LANGUAGE js.

The UPDATE_SECURITY authorization check added to the polyglot engine is not reached by the SQL function-definition, registration, and library-function invocation route; these surfaces lack a scripting-permission check.
Invocation of the defined SQL library function executes the supplied JavaScript despite the caller lacking the security-admin permission intended to restrict scripting.

The caller bypasses the scripting authorization control; although Java host lookup/reflection is described as blocked on this path, IOAccess.ALL permits load(url), enabling remote JavaScript inclusion or SSRF, and JavaScript can consume unbounded CPU or memory.

failure.operation: SQLQueryEngine library-function invocation of a JavaScript function created through DefineFunctionStatement.executeSimple

primary_invariant.statement: Every SQL or polyglot route that defines, invokes, or deletes JavaScript/polyglot user code must enforce UPDATE_SECURITY before allowing that operation.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The existing permission gate was placed only on the polyglot engine route, while SQL DEFINE FUNCTION, function-library registration, and SQL library-function invocation could reach JavaScript execution without that gate.

quality.review_notes: Mechanism, request shape, and remediation are grounded in the GitHub-reviewed OSV details and upstream advisory. No immutable patch diff, source checkout, or recorded probe/test execution is present; the HTTP oracle is a proposed harness contract rather than an observed result.

remediation.invariant_restored: A centralized assertCanExecuteUserCode(database) authorization decision is invoked by every code-execution surface, including SQL definition, invocation (including pre-existing libraries), and deletion for js/polyglot languages; the execution context is further restricted with IOAccess.NONE and PolyglotAccess.NONE.
mitigation_classes: centralized authorization enforcement for user-code execution
permission checks on SQL function definition, invocation, and deletion
disable polyglot I/O and host access

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Affected versions are versions prior to 26.7.2, including listed releases through 26.7.1.

target.component: SQL function definition and library-function invocation paths to the JavaScript/polyglot engine

oracle.channel: HTTP command endpoint followed by SQL invocation
oracle.expected_negative: On the fixed release, the same non-security-admin caller should be denied on the covered JavaScript/polyglot definition, invocation, or deletion surface.
oracle.expected_positive: On an affected version, a database-authorized caller lacking UPDATE_SECURITY can submit DEFINE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE js and invoke the function through SELECT.
